key_insight: Magnetic transition-metal oxides can exhibit intrinsic band gaps without long-range magnetic order or an explicit strong-correlation mechanism when local symmetry breaking is allowed.
engineering_relevance: Local magnetic motifs offer a route to modeling insulating oxide phases without relying on an adjustable Hubbard U parameter.
method: Use parameter-free, mean-field-like density functional theory with energy-lowering symmetry breaking.
Represent antiferromagnetic and paramagnetic phases through local magnetic motifs.
Electronically isolate magnetic motifs using wide-gap barriers, including NiO6 octahedra embedded in MgO.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that electronically isolated magnetic motifs retain intrinsic band gaps even as long-range magnetic order vanishes, but provides no numerical gap values or error metrics.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish quantitative accuracy across oxide chemistries or realistic finite-temperature paramagnetic states.
paper_title: Metallic or insulating magnetic phases of transition-metal oxides in light of the Slater vs Mott controversy
